messages:
Maya (Support): Customer reports intermittent 401s right after rotating an API key via the console. They rotated the key (old id ak-98 -> new ak-99) and then saw 401s from one of their pods to our API. Sample header: x-redwood-request-id: req_12345. They did NOT restart their pods. Can eng confirm expected propagation behavior and recommended repro steps? :eyes:

Sam (Eng): do we know whether they used the built-in rotate flow (server-side revoke + issue new) or manually revoked? If server-side rotate, revocation marks old key inactive immediately. Validation is stateless on our side, so 401s mean the client is still presenting the old key. Need exact key id and a sample failing request. Also: do they mount secret as env var or via sidecar/volume?

Maya (Support): They used the console rotate flow. Old key ak-98, new ak-99. They use a k8s secrets-syncer that writes to /etc/secrets/api_key inside the container. Customer says the file sometimes updates but the app still returns 401 for ~45s then recovers. Repro they provided: rotate in console -> observe pod logs -> curl inside pod returns 401 for a few dozen seconds.

Henry (SRE): I checked audit traces: Vault audit shows secret version increment at 1768000980, and our key-service logged revocation at 1768000984. There was a cluster leader failover on the customer's control plane around the same time which might delay the syncer. Important: our secrets-syncer only sends a reload signal if the deployment has the annotation secrets-syncer/reload-on-change: 'true'. If that's missing, file may update but app won't reload. Also some apps read into memory at startup and never re-check the file.

Kevin (DevEx): Short-term workaround: restart the process or deployment. For example: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<app-name>. For testing rotation quickly you can run: ```
# from a node or debug pod
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <OLD_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# expect 401 after rotation
```
If the file updates but app doesn't, that's a client-side behaviour. :lock:

VaultBot: Secret 'redwood/apikeys/ak-99' created (audit event). Policy=rw. TTL=none.

Sam (Eng): From server-side tracing, we make no per-request cache of key material — validation consults the active key set each request. So the old key returning 401 implies the client process is still sending ak-98. Two diagnostic checks for the customer: 1) kubectl exec -it <pod> -- cat /etc/secrets/api_key to confirm file contents; 2) inside the process, check env / in-memory copy. If the file shows ak-99 but the process env shows ak-98, app needs restart or a reload hook.

Maya (Support): Customer ran kubectl exec and confirmed the file had ak-99 immediately after rotation, but their app was still using ak-98 (they read into memory at startup). They want no restarts in production. Any zero-downtime suggestions? :thinking_face:

Henry (SRE): Patterns for zero-downtime rotation: use a small sidecar that watches the file and signals the main process (SIGHUP or HTTP kiss-of-death) when secret changes; or use CSI driver / projected volume with automount so kubelet updates volume and process can be signaled. Another option: issue short-lived tokens to pods (ephemeral) so rotation only affects new tokens. For now, advise the customer to implement a hot-reload path or use a sidecar. For an immediate fix: kubectl patch deployment <app> -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rotatedAt":"$(date +%s)"}}}}}' will trigger a rolling restart without changing image.

Sam (Eng): I'll create a short DevEx doc with example sidecar code and kubectl patterns. Also will add a telemetry check to surface increased 401 rates during rotation so support can detect this automatically. Planning to follow up with a PR to our docs repo. :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): Customer accepted the rolling restart workaround and asked whether Redwood Console could optionally emit a webhook on key rotation so their platform could trigger reloads. Can we consider an outbound hook on rotation events?

Kevin (DevEx): That makes sense as a product feature — rotation webhook per project or per-key would let infra teams implement automated reloads. I'll open a feature request and sketch the spec (include HMAC signature, retry policy).

DeployBot: Created ticket INC-2147 (feature: rotation-webhook) and linked it to this thread.

Maya (Support): Closing loop for now: advised customer to either implement hot-reload sidecar or accept a rolling restart as immediate mitigation. Logged repro steps (rotate via console -> cat /etc/secrets/api_key -> verify process env -> restart if necessary). We'll follow up once DevEx has a doc/PR. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
